results.summary: This design is an accumulator-based 8-bit microarchitecture developed entirely through GPT-4 conversations. It uses a scan chain accessible via SPI to load programs and read processor state. An external microcontroller with SPI is required to program and run the processor. The design is notable for being generated by GPT-4 and includes a full ISA with arithmetic, logic, and branching instructions.

This design provides a PWM generator and a PWM reader. The generator's duty cycle is set by input pins, and the reader's output is reflected on output pins. An SPI interface allows configuration and readback. It is designed for a 20ms period with duty cycles between 1ms and 2ms, typical for servo control.

ChipTune implements an 8-bit Programmable Sound Generator inspired by vintage video game APUs. It accepts commands via a UART interface at 9600 baud and outputs PWM audio. The design includes two square wave generators, a triangle wave generator, and a noise generator, each with configurable parameters. External hardware required is a computer COM port and an analog PWM filter with audio amplifier.

This design implements an 8-bit signed Baugh-Wooley multiplier. The two operands are loaded via input pins, and the 16-bit product is available after one clock cycle. No external hardware is required. It is a straightforward arithmetic block suitable for DSP applications.

This design implements a 60 Hz grid-forming inverter controller using a CORDIC algorithm to generate a sine wave reference. It includes PWM modulators for an H-bridge and a dump load, and uses ADC inputs to monitor AC and DC voltages. The controller adjusts the dump load to regulate the DC link voltage. It requires external power electronics including an H-bridge, transformer, and solar panel system.

Solo Squash is a one-player VGA game that bounces a ball within a playfield with three walls and a paddle. The player controls the paddle with up/down buttons to keep the ball in play. It generates VGA video signals (640x480) and simple audio tones on bounces. External hardware required are resistors for VGA output, pushbuttons, and optionally a speaker.

This is a simple 4-bit current output DAC. It takes a 4-bit digital input on the digital pins and sinks a corresponding current on the analog pin. It requires an external resistive load on the analog output. The design is analog and transistor-level, with no clock.

This design implements a stepper motor controller using a Moore state machine. It supports three step types (full, half, double) and two directions, with four selectable speeds based on a time base derived from the 50MHz clock. The outputs are four phase signals (I1-I4) to drive the motor. It requires an external FPGA or test setup with switches for control inputs.

This project is a simple introduction to Tiny Tapeout using Wokwi. It implements a few AND gates with 8 inputs and 4 outputs. The documentation is minimal, stating the author is still figuring it out. It can be tested with dip switches and a 7-segment display. It serves as a learning template.
This project is a placeholder test for the Tiny Tapeout workflow. It has no functional description and no pin assignments. It is intended as a learning exercise. No external hardware is required.
